name: VERTICAL AUTOCLAVE STERILIZER
desc: Vertical Laboratory Autoclave Sterilizer engineered for high-performance steam sterilization of medical instruments, culture media, and glassware. Features a robust 75-liter vertical chamber fabricated entirely from high-grade Stainless Steel 304.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS VERTICAL AUTOCLAVE STERILIZER operates on the principle of saturated steam sterilization under high pressure, where purified water is heated inside a sealed 75-liter Stainless Steel 304 chamber to generate steam at pressures above atmospheric level, raising the boiling point of water and delivering latent heat of vaporization directly to all exposed surfaces of the load. This moist heat irreversibly denatures microbial enzymes, structural proteins, and nucleic acids, destroying vegetative bacteria, fungi, viruses, and highly resistant bacterial endospores such as Geobacillus stearothermophilus and Bacillus subtilis, thereby achieving the sterility assurance levels specified in ISO 17665 and pharmacopoeial moist-heat sterilization standards. In clinical and research laboratories, doctors use this sterilizer to process wrapped surgical instruments, scalpels, forceps, and dressing packs; B.Sc and M.Sc students sterilize nutrient agar, potato dextrose agar, broth media, pipette tips, petri dishes, and contaminated glassware; PhD researchers, biotechnologists, and chemists sterilize bioreactor parts, culture flasks, membrane filters, media bottles, and biohazard laboratory waste before disposal. The advanced microprocessor-based digital PID temperature controller precisely regulates the thermal profile from ambient to 126°C, ensuring stable saturated-steam conditions, validated cycle repeatability, and compliance with good laboratory and infection-control practices.
sop: Ensure the autoclave is connected to a 230 V AC, 50 Hz single-phase supply and fill the SS304 chamber with distilled or purified water up to the manufacturer-recommended level.

Load sterilizable materials such as culture media, glassware, or wrapped surgical instruments into the chamber with adequate spacing for steam circulation; loosen caps and open pipette tip boxes if applicable.
Close the lid and engage the heavy-duty radial lock assembly completely, verifying that the high-temperature silicone rubber gasket is seated uniformly and no foreign material is trapped.
Switch ON the main power supply; the digital PID temperature controller will illuminate and display the current chamber temperature or process value.
Use the 'UP' and 'DOWN' arrows to adjust to the required target parameter, typically 121°C for standard media and instruments or up to 126°C for heat-stable loads.
Press 'SET' again to lock the value; the controller will automatically energize the industrial heating elements and maintain the programmed set point throughout the cycle.

Monitor the analogue pressure gauge on the top lid until it reaches approximately 15 psi (103 kPa), corresponding to 121°C saturated steam, and confirm that the spring-loaded safety valve is not continuously releasing steam.
Maintain the sterilization dwell time for 15–20 minutes after the chamber reaches the target temperature, or as validated for the specific load type and biological indicator requirements.
After the cycle is complete, allow the chamber pressure to drop naturally to zero and the temperature to fall below 80°C before attempting to open the lid; if a venting valve is used, open it slowly.

Wear heat-resistant gloves and open the lid away from your face, remove the sterilized items carefully, place them on a clean heat-resistant cart or tray, and allow them to cool and dry before storage or use.

CRITICAL SAFETY WARNING: Never attempt to open the autoclave while the pressure gauge reads above zero or the digital display is above 80°C, and never autoclave sealed volatile solvents, flammable liquids, strong acids, chlorine-releasing compounds, or sealed airtight containers, as these can cause violent rupture, explosive vapor release, or toxic exposure; always use biological and chemical indicators to verify each cycle before relying on the sterilized load.
